A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARM research, with matching methods and retained experiments despite the changed title and organization. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original ARM detoxification and sentiment-control results, component ablations, generated examples, and decoding-time measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original ARM experiments and adds LLaMA-2 evaluations, alternative evaluation metrics, and empirical matrix-factorization and representational-capacity tests.

M1.justification: The baseline-plus-bilinear reward head, supervised and distillation objectives, sampled-token regularization, and guided decoding procedure are retained. The low-rank formulation analyzes the existing parameterization; rewritten equations and additional backbone configurations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: The Jigsaw/RealToxicityPrompts detoxification and Amazon Polarity/SST-2/OpenWebText sentiment coverage remains unchanged. Appendix C.1 adds a synthetic 1024-by-1024 identity-matrix fitting task to test reward-model capacity.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 3 adds GeDi and DExperts to the current-Perspective-API detoxification comparison; v1 Figure 2 compared ARM with RAD and unguided GPT-2. Their older-API scores remain separately displayed, and the sentiment comparator set is retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds LLaMA-2-7b/13b generators with TinyLLaMA reward models and OLMo perplexity evaluation, MAUVE measurements using 1000 prompts, and RoBERTa toxicity scoring. It also introduces synthetic fitting and numerical-rank protocols and extends the timing experiment's top-k range from 40 to 80. Existing GPT-2 benchmark settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: Figures 1, 5, and 7 and Appendices B–C add substantial rank, matrix-fitting, and capacity analyses. V2 also checks toxicity findings across evaluators. The original fluency/toxicity component ablation remains, while v1 Figure 5's sorted next-token reward-distribution analysis is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training seeds, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both retain 25 sampled continuations per prompt; v2 introduces no corresponding uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All original metric values in Tables 2–3 are retained, with MAUVE added. V2 adds LLaMA-2, RoBERTa-scored, and rank/factorization results; for example, Table 4 reports ARM/LLaMA-2-7b at beta 100 with toxicity 0.142 and MAUVE 0.95. Figure 6 replaces timing values, but v1's unspecified hardware prevents a same-setting speed comparison.

T1.justification: Section 3 introduces the reward-matrix definition, a matrix-completion reformulation, and ARM's rank bound. Appendices A–C add a weighted-mean minimizer proof, a rank-one completion construction, and a synthetic reconstruction-error bound. These are substantial formal additions beyond v1's method equations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion newly elevate reward-matrix analysis and RAD's apparently unused representational flexibility to central contributions. The original claim that ARM offers efficient guidance with quality comparable to RAD remains.

C2.justification: V2 interprets low rank through sparse observations and connects regularization to reduced output rank. It newly distinguishes observed low-rank fits from the unknown true reward matrix, discusses possible neglect of rare prefixes, and questions whether some toxicity patterns require higher rank. The earlier general safety limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds alternating-least-squares settings, numerical-rank cutoffs, MAUVE implementation details, evaluator/backbone access information, and RTX A6000 timing hardware. Existing optimizer, batch-size, and task-training schedules are largely retained. These additions substantially expand reproduction guidance for the new analyses and evaluations.

R1.justification: V2 positions ARM through matrix completion and the softmax bottleneck, adding connections to Mazumder et al., Hastie et al., Yang et al., and Finlayson et al. It adds evaluation/model references and removes several earlier contextual citations. This substantively expands the research framing beyond v1's comparison of discriminator and language-model guidance.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around low rank. Guided decoding becomes a preliminaries section, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5 and is rewritten, training explanations are consolidated, and the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 adds rank and evaluation figures, expands benchmark plots with MAUVE panels, restructures the ablation display, and redraws the timing plot. Tables gain MAUVE columns and new model/evaluator results. The unchanged generated-example tables are consolidated onto a rotated final page.

improvement.justification: LLaMA-2 testing, MAUVE, open-weight toxicity checks, and current-API GeDi/DExperts comparisons strengthen empirical support and reproducibility. However, the new central formalization needs correction: Section 3.1's unweighted Frobenius objective omits aggregate observation weights, and Section 3.2 conflates zero-filled matrix rank with completion rank. The stronger empirical checks provide a limited net improvement despite these theoretical issues.
